newsitem.title: USA: Scripps to buy Harte-Hanks properties.
newsitem.headline: Scripps to buy Harte-Hanks properties.

text.p: E.W. Scripps Co. said on Monday it agreed to buy six newspapers, a television station and a radio station from Harte-Hanks Communications Inc. for between $605 million and $625 million, mostly in stock.

Scripps said the deal would result in about 5 percent dilution to its earnings in the first year, but should add to profits by the second or third year. Scripps also authorised the repurchase on the open market of as many of its shares as are issued to Harte-Hanks.

The newspapers are the Corpus Christi Caller-Times, the Abilene Reporter-News, the Wichita Falls Times Record News and the San Angelo Standard-Times, all in Texas; and the Anderson (S.C.) Independent Mail.

Scripps also agreed to acquire KENS-TV, a CBS affiliate in San Antonio; its sister radio station KENS-AM; and a group of non-daily suburban community newspapers in the Dallas area. With the purchase, Scripps will have newspapers in 22 markets and a total of 10 television stations.

Scripps said the deal is structured as a tax-free "Morris Trust" transaction, with the financial details dependent upon the amount of debt the acquired properties carry. If there is no debt to be assumed, then Harte-Hanks gets $605 million, all in stock. With assumed debt, the potential value of the deal goes to $625 million, it said.
If a "Morris Trust" deal turns out not to be feasible tax-free due to pending federal legislation, then Scripps will pay Harte-Hanks $775 million in cash, the company said.
